email.scenario: You recently attended a workshop on drought-tolerant plants at your local environmental center. Afterward, you emailed the workshop coordinator to request the session's sensor data handout, but the file you received will not open.

Explain that the sensor data attachment will not open.
Ask the coordinator to resend the handout as a PDF or spreadsheet.

academicDiscussion.professorPost: Some companies have begun setting aside a quiet room where employees can take a short rest during the workday as part of a broader wellbeing initiative. Supporters say brief rest breaks improve focus and reduce fatigue, while critics worry about fairness when some employees end up covering for those who are away. Do you think workplaces should offer a dedicated nap room? Why or why not?

studentPosts.name: Marcus
studentPosts.post: I think a nap room is a smart investment. A short rest in the afternoon can restore attention and lower stress, especially in jobs that demand long stretches of concentration. Employees who return refreshed usually work more accurately and make fewer costly mistakes, so the time away more than pays for itself.

studentPosts.name: Elena
studentPosts.post: I'm not convinced. When one person naps, someone else often has to cover phones or handle walk-ins, and that resentment builds quickly on a small team. A workplace should protect everyone's working time equally rather than offer a break that some employees can use and others can't because their role doesn't allow it.
